channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Falls Short of Votes for International Civil Aviation Organization Council Seat
item.description: Kazakhstan did not secure enough votes to gain a seat on the Council of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). The country was vying for representation within the global aviation governing body, but ultimately fell short in the election.

item.title: Taliban Reportedly Pardons Convicted Criminals Under 'Compassion' Decree
item.description: Sources claim the Taliban are releasing or reducing sentences for convicted criminals, particularly group members or their relatives, under a decree of 'compassion' from leader Hibatullah Akhundzada. Recent releases and sentence reductions occurred in Kandahar.

item.title: Kazakhstan exported $327.8 million in gold to Kyrgyzstan in nine months
item.description: Kazakhstan exported $327.8 million worth of gold to Kyrgyzstan in the first nine months of 2026. This represents 98.5% of the total exports for the entire year 2025. Kyrgyzstan remains the largest buyer of Kazakh gold, although its share of total exports decreased slightly.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prohibits Business Inspections Based on Anonymous Complaints
item.description: Uzbekistan will prohibit inspections of businesses based on anonymous complaints, according to a new draft law. The legislation, titled "On State Control of Entrepreneurial Entities," also includes other significant measures aimed at protecting entrepreneurs' rights. This reform seeks to create a more favorable environment for business operations in the country.

item.title: Almaty Rescuers Survey 73 High-Risk Landslide Areas in One Day
item.description: In Almaty, rescuers and city officials inspected 73 areas prone to landslides within a single day. The operation, involving 72 emergency service personnel, focused on the Bostandyk, Medeu, and Nauryzbai districts. Residents were informed about recognizing landslide threats and evacuation procedures.

item.title: International Equestrian Federation President Visits Astana for Official Engagement
item.description: Ingmar De Vos, President of the International Equestrian Federation (FEI), arrived in Astana for an official visit. The visit aims to strengthen Kazakhstan's cooperation with the international equestrian community, enhance its global standing, and explore new partnership avenues. Discussions will focus on future collaboration, international sports agendas, and infrastructure development.

item.title: Tajikistan and Toloka Explore Establishing an AI Research Laboratory
item.description: Tajikistan and international tech company Toloka are considering establishing a specialized AI research laboratory in Tajikistan. Discussions focused on data annotation and labeling for AI model training, potential joint initiatives at the A7LAS AI industrial park, and developing infrastructure for applied AI projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Water-Saving Technologies Over Siberian Water Transfer Project
item.description: Uzbekistan deems investing in water-saving technologies more beneficial than a costly Siberian water transfer project estimated at $100 billion. The Ministry of Water Resources reported saving 10.69 billion cubic meters of water in 2026 through modern irrigation and canal improvements, requiring significantly less investment.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Para-Judo Team Secures Five Medals at Egypt Grand Prix
item.description: Uzbekistan's para-judo athletes achieved significant success at the IBSA Grand Prix in Alexandria, Egypt, winning a total of five medals. The team secured two gold, one silver, and two bronze medals on the first day of the competition, with athletes excelling in both J1 and J2 classes.

item.title: Woman Brutally Murdered and Dismembered in Ghor Province
item.description: Local sources report the brutal murder of a woman in the Pasht-e Noor area of Dawlatyar District, Ghor Province. The incident reportedly occurred four days prior to the report. The victim's body parts were dismembered after her death. Details regarding the victim's identity and the perpetrators remain unavailable.

item.title: Experts predict a decline in oil prices in December
item.description: Experts from the company "Euler" predict a further decrease in oil prices in December, attributing it to the recovery of oil exports from the Middle East. Despite China's increased oil imports, prices have fallen due to rising export volumes from the region, restoring market balance.

item.title: OIC contact group discusses roadmap for engaging with Afghanistan's authorities
item.description: The OIC Ministerial Contact Group on Afghanistan held a technical meeting in Jeddah to discuss a roadmap for phased engagement with the country's authorities. The plan aims to guide constructive dialogue on shared interests, address political and humanitarian situations, and promote stability and development in Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan seizes over 200 kg of drugs and arrests 35 people in 10 days
item.description: Kazakh authorities have seized over 200 kilograms of drugs and arrested 35 individuals in the first ten days of November. Significant drug busts occurred in Almaty, Shymkent, and Pavlodar, including large quantities of ketamine, synthetic drugs, and mephedrone. One woman was apprehended for attempting to distribute drugs as a courier.

item.title: Uzbek Bank Employee Embezzles Over $250,000 in Client Funds for Online Gambling
item.description: An employee of a bank in Andijan, Uzbekistan, has been arrested for embezzling over 3.2 billion soums (approximately $250,000) from client accounts. The funds were used for online gambling. The suspect confessed and faces charges of embezzlement. This follows similar crackdowns on illegal financial operations in Tashkent.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Algeria Agree to Launch Regular Flights Between Countries
item.description: Kazakhstan and Algeria have signed a memorandum to establish regular flights, allowing up to 14 flights per week for designated airlines of each country. The agreement was reached at the ICAO World Aviation Transport Conference in Montreal.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expert Discusses Nuances of Freedom of Conscience
item.description: A PhD candidate in religious studies and director at Astana Open Dialogue discusses the growing public debate in Kazakhstan surrounding religious preachers and bloggers. Concerns include their influence on citizens' worldviews, the opposition of music and art to religion, and the subordinate role assigned to women.

item.title: Uzbekistan: A New Key Partner for the United States in Central Asia?
item.description: Uzbekistan is attracting increasing interest from the United States amid regional rivalries and energy concerns. Washington aims to strengthen ties with this pivotal Central Asian actor, potentially reshaping the geopolitical landscape. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit with a large business delegation highlights this growing engagement.

item.title: Turkmenistan Secures Nearly $100 Million in Trade Deals with Afghan and UAE Buyers
item.description: Turkmenistan recorded transactions worth approximately $99.2 million and $947,250 on November 17. Afghan entrepreneurs agreed to purchase refined cottonseed oil for export, while UAE buyers signed deals for unbleached fabric. Local businesses also purchased petroleum road bitumen.

item.title: Another Uzbek Citizen Suspected of Fraud Arrested in Turkey
item.description: An Uzbek citizen, suspected of defrauding individuals of significant assets, has been apprehended in Turkey. The individual is accused of obtaining substantial property through deceitful means. Following their arrest, the person was deported from Turkey.

item.title: Driver arrested for dangerous drifting in Astana without a license, sentenced to 20 days
item.description: A 22-year-old driver in Astana was arrested and sentenced to 20 days in administrative detention for dangerous drifting and driving without a license. The driver performed risky maneuvers on a city street, damaging the road surface. The car owner also faces responsibility.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Remains Georgia's Top Market Despite 40.7% Export Drop
item.description: Kyrgyzstan maintained its position as Georgia's largest export market in January-October 2026, despite a 40.7% decrease in exports to $731.5 million. Cars accounted for over 95% of this trade. Georgia's overall exports grew by 17.9% during the same period.

item.title: Taliban Dispute UN Report on Increased Opium Cultivation in Afghanistan
item.description: The Islamic Emirate disputes a UN report estimating a sharp increase in opium poppy cultivation to over 43,000 hectares in 2026. The Ministry of Interior claims its counter-narcotics operations have reduced cultivation to near zero, destroying crops on 23,000 hectares.

item.title: Drone Attacks Injure 10 at Tribal Peace Gathering in Pakistan
item.description: Two drone attacks targeted a tribal peace gathering in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on November 22, injuring at least 10 people. The gathering was intended to discuss security concerns and peace restoration. Police reported the injured were taken to Bannu District Headquarters Hospital. The attacks highlight growing concerns over drone use in militant violence.

item.title: European Commission: Europe's Military Readiness Plans Under Threat
item.description: A leaked draft European Commission work program indicates Europe's goal of full military readiness by 2030 is under threat. Despite political will and increased defense spending, the EU faces significant security challenges and hybrid threats. The document highlights persistent gaps in European military capabilities.

item.title: New Tashkent: A Planned City for Up to Two Million Residents Under Construction
item.description: A new city, 'New Tashkent,' designed for up to two million residents, is under construction on the eastern outskirts of Uzbekistan's capital. Launched in 2023, the project aims to be a major economic and administrative center spanning 20,000 hectares. The first phase will house 600,000 people.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Visit Jordan on November 23
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Jordan on November 23 at the invitation of the Jordanian King. The visit will include high-level negotiations, a business forum, and other events aimed at strengthening bilateral ties.

item.title: California Investigates Nvidia Over Suspected Technology Leak to China
item.description: California authorities have launched an investigation into Nvidia concerning the potential transfer of advanced chips and confidential information to China. The state's Attorney General is also examining if the company misled investors about China-related risks. Nvidia has been issued a subpoena for information regarding potential violations of corporate security laws.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Visit Jordan for Talks and Agreements
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev is scheduled to visit Jordan for high-level negotiations aimed at forging new agreements. The visit is part of ongoing diplomatic efforts to strengthen bilateral ties and explore areas of mutual cooperation between the two nations.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev to Visit Jordan for State Visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will undertake a state visit to the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan on November 23-24, accepting an invitation from King Abdullah II. The visit includes high-level talks in Amman, a business forum, and discussions on expanding trade, economic, and investment cooperation. Special focus will be on sectors like textiles, mining, agriculture, and pharmaceuticals.

item.title: Iranian Attack Causes Fire at Bahrain Industrial Site, Tehran Claims US Base Strikes
item.description: An Iranian attack struck an industrial facility in Bahrain on Saturday, November 21, causing a fire and material damage but no casualties. Bahrain's Interior Ministry reported the incident as Iranian aggression. Simultaneously, Iran's IRGC claimed responsibility for missile and drone operations targeting US military positions in Bahrain.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Sindarov to Challenge India's Gukesh for World Chess Title
item.description: Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov, 20, will challenge India's Gukesh Dommaraju, also 20, for the World Chess Championship. This match features the youngest combined age of any two contenders in classical chess history. Gukesh defends his title won in 2024, while Sindarov qualified by winning the 2026 FIDE Candidates Tournament. The match begins November 24.

item.title: Kazakhstan Fails to Secure Seat on ICAO Council After Election
item.description: Kazakhstan did not secure a seat on the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Council in its first attempt, finishing fifth among six candidates with 78 out of 158 votes. The election took place in Montreal during the 43rd ICAO Assembly session. Kazakhstan fell short by 32 votes to secure one of the four additional seats.

item.title: Afghanistan Faces Chronic Leadership Crisis Amidst Political Failures and Lack of Vision
item.description: Afghanistan's political history is marked by a persistent leadership crisis, lacking figures with deep political understanding and foresight. The recent speech by Taliban Supreme Leader Mullah Hibatullah Akhundzada at Kabul University offered no clear message or plan to address the nation's poverty, unemployment, and despair, highlighting the ongoing absence of leaders prioritizing national interests.

item.title: Taliban Announce 481 People, Including 92 Families, Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban reported that 92 families, totaling 481 individuals, were forcibly returned to Afghanistan through various border crossings. Deputy spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat stated that significant numbers entered via Torkham and Silk Bridge, with others returning through Spin Boldak and Islam Qala.

item.title: Taliban Declare 600 Acres of Balkh Town Land as "Emirati"
item.description: The Taliban have declared approximately 600 acres of land in a town in Balkh province as "Emirati." This action signifies a change in land ownership and administration under Taliban rule.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister to Attend ECO Summit in Tehran
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, the Taliban's acting foreign minister, will attend the 18th Summit of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in Tehran on December 3-4. The summit will focus on regional economic cooperation, trade, and transit. Notably, the Taliban was not invited to the previous ECO summit in Islamabad.

item.title: Bishkek Wastewater Treatment Plant Undergoing Major Renovation and Modernization
item.description: Bishkek's wastewater treatment plant is being renovated across 50 hectares. The project, a public-private partnership, includes replacing equipment, implementing automated control, and energy-efficient solutions. Plans also involve installing solar panels and an odor control system. The facility, built in 1976-1980, serves Bishkek and nearby areas.

item.title: Iran Parliament Deputy Speaker Accuses Trump of Fabricating Drone Figures
item.description: Iran's Parliament Deputy Speaker Hamidreza Haji-Babaei claims US President Trump is fabricating drone figures to hide US military casualties. He stated that countries losing in competition often resort to fake statistics. Haji-Babaei asserted Iran had captured enemy drones and acquired advanced underwater military equipment.

item.title: US Senator Calls for Oversight on AI Use in War Against Iran
item.description: US Senator Kirsten Gillibrand has warned about the risks of using artificial intelligence in the war against Iran without human oversight. She called for an investigation, stating that AI is effective in intercepting missiles but lack of human control could endanger civilians, citing a school attack.

item.title: US Could Face Bankruptcy if Debt Ceiling Issue Not Resolved, Warns Trump
item.description: President Donald Trump stated that the United States could face a financial crisis and bankruptcy if the debt ceiling issue is not resolved. He proposed completely removing the statutory debt limit, citing concerns about its use as a political tool.
